passage: Hybrid work reduces the number of routine commuting trips for many employees, but the net transport effect is not automatically proportional. Some households move farther from workplaces when daily attendance is no longer required. Others use saved commuting time for additional non-work journeys. Office energy use may also remain high when buildings serve fewer people on any given day. These rebound effects do not erase the potential benefit of hybrid work; they show why evaluations must include residential choices, trip substitution and building operation rather than counting avoided commutes alone.
